clue.text: 1000 smack dealers with time off for good behaviour

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for 1000

indicators.note: off here means the letter for time is taken away from the dealers

parts.note: tanners deal out a smack, since to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: Drug dealers getting their prison sentence cut for behaving well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' looks like heroin, but here it means a beating: tanners are people who give someone a tanning. Taking T out of TANNERS leaves ANNERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Manners are polite conduct, which is what good behaviour means.

clue.text: In haze, bag up, but put in the wrong hams?

indicators.note: In means the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: mist is a haze

indicators.note: in a down answer up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sac is a bag-like pouch in the body

explanation.surface: A shopper in a fog who has bagged up the wrong joints of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hams' are not meat but bad actors, and 'up' works because this is a down answer, read from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: To miscast is to give actors unsuitable roles, and hams are overacting performers.

clue.text: A bottom one couldn't possibly get beneath?

definitions.text: A bottom one couldn't possibly get beneath?

parts.words: A bottom one couldn't possibly get beneath?
parts.note: the lowest point of all, which nothing can go below

explanation.surface: A seat or backside you can't possibly get under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom' suggests a backside, but it means the lowest point.
explanation.definitionFit: A nadir is the very lowest point, so nothing can sink lower than it.

clue.text: Topless chap having 45 mins with mature escort

indicators.note: topless means the word loses its first letter, its top in a down answer

parts.note: gent, short for gentleman, means a chap
45 minutes is three quarters of an hour, so three of the four letters of hour
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A shirtless man spending three quarters of an hour with an older escort.
explanation.walkthrough: '45 mins' is three quarters of HOUR, giving OUR. 'Topless' cuts G from GENT, leaving ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is the group of attendants who accompany an important person, so it is a kind of escort.

clue.text: Dope mostly found in Stone shot full of barbiturates

indicators.note: found in means the first piece sits inside the second

parts.note: a stone is the seed of a fruit such as a cherry

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: dope is slang for information, data

explanation.surface: Drugs found in a cannabis plant that has sprouted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' looks like a drug but means information, and 'Stone shot' is not the definition: 'shot full of barbiturates' is.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sedated has been calmed with drugs such as barbiturates, which are classic sedatives.

clue.text: Tumbler drunk actor filled with Bass and drop of Armagnac

indicators.note: filled with means the other letters are put inside the jumbled word
a drunk actor is unsteady and muddled, so the letters of actor get jumbled

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bass, the singer's voice part

indicators.note: a drop of something is a tiny bit, so this takes the first letter of Armagnac

explanation.surface: An actor who has had too much beer and brandy is falling over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' scrambles ACTOR into ACROT, and 'filled with' puts B and A inside it. Bass is also a brand of beer, which suits the drinking scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbler is an acrobat who does somersaults and flips.

clue.text: Trouble at work with Her Maj in a flap

indicators.note: the monarch is placed in the middle of the other letters

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
on means working, as a machine that is on
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Trouble at work leaves the Queen in a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flap' looks like a panic but means a hinged wing part. ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: An aileron is a hinged flap on an aircraft wing that controls roll.

clue.text: Waterway in Phoenix?

parts.note: a natural waterway that is also the first name of a Hollywood actor surnamed Phoenix

explanation.surface: Asking about a canal in the Arizona city of Phoenix.
explanation.walkthrough: Phoenix looks like the city in Arizona, but it is the surname of the actor River Phoenix.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a natural waterway, and River was the first name of the actor Phoenix.

clue.text: Red robin lad released close to gazebo

indicators.note: letters that are released are set free, so they can move into a new order
the close of a word is its end, so the last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A boy setting free a robin near the summerhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' looks like the robin's breast, but it is a red wine. 'released' rearranges ROBIN LAD and 'close to' adds O.
explanation.definitionFit: Bardolino is a light red wine from near Lake Garda in Italy.

clue.text: Old jailers ignoring last of warden's failures

indicators.note: ignoring means one letter is left out

parts.note: turnkey is an old word for a jailer, the one who turned the key

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Old prison guards who don't take any notice of the warden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' drops N, the last letter of warden, from TURNKEYS.
explanation.definitionFit: A turkey is slang for a flop, especially a play or film that fails badly.

clue.text: Who cares if princess punches drunk?

indicators.note: punches means one piece is pushed right into the other

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
Di was the popular name for Diana, Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: Someone shrugging off the idea of a princess hitting a drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: So do it is a casual exclamation of not caring, like saying never mind or whatever.

clue.text: One closely involved with Labour Lord

definitions.meaning: someone who delivers babies, a midwife, is closely involved with a woman's labour
the Lord is called the ... because he saves and rescues his people

explanation.surface: A politician who is deeply involved with the Labour Party and sits in the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is the UK's main left-wing party, which makes 'Labour' look political. Here it means childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: Midwives deliver babies, and God in scripture is the rescuer of His people.

clue.text: An insubstantial axe?

parts.note: axe is slang for a guitar, and one made of nothing at all is mimed by a fan playing along to rock music

explanation.surface: An axe that has no real substance.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock musicians call a guitar an axe. One with no substance is the instrument a fan pretends to strum.
explanation.definitionFit: Miming wild guitar playing with empty hands means playing an instrument that is not really there.

clue.text: 6-1 … right, Hearts must be in the lead!

indicators.note: the two letters go at the front, ahead of what the number gives

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hearts, the card suit
the figure 1 is written out as the word one

explanation.surface: A betting tip at odds of six to one: Hearts, the Edinburgh football club, will be winning.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' refers to the answer of 6 Down, RIVER, so the definition is a river. '6-1' looks like odds, but the 1 gives ONE, with R and H in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhone is a major river in Switzerland and France that flows into the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Will group of lawyers bow to DA?

parts.note: the Bar is the body of barristers as a whole

indicators.note: the bow is the front of a ship, so the bow of DA is its first letter

explanation.surface: Will the lawyers give way to a district attorney?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like the start of a question but is the definition: Will Shakespeare. 'bow to' looks like deference; a ship's bow is its front, so it takes the first letter of DA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bard is the nickname of William Shakespeare, so it stands for Will.

clue.text: Worldly-wise Hoskins is one hot to open shaken-up lager tin

indicators.note: to open means the letter goes into the middle of the jumbled word
a shaken-up can has its contents jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: The setter, said to be streetwise, cracking open a shaken can of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worldly-wise' means as far as worlds go: the setter is a native of Earth. 'to open' puts H into the scrambled LAGER TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthling is an inhabitant of Earth, as anyone from this world is.

clue.text: Academic rejected passes for dunces

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer
to pass away is to die, so passes means dies

explanation.surface: A lecturer turning down pass marks for the slowest students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passes' looks like exam results, but it means dies. DON read backwards gives NOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A noddy is an old word for a simpleton or fool, so noddies are dunces.

clue.text: Unfortunately, ginger dad can be humiliating

indicators.note: something going unfortunately goes wrong, so the letters fall out of order

explanation.surface: A red-haired father who sadly embarrasses his children.
explanation.definitionFit: Degrading treatment lowers someone's dignity, which is what humiliating means.

clue.text: Predict death will come after strong wine

indicators.note: the word for death is placed after the word for wine

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
end means death, as in meeting one's end

explanation.surface: A warning that heavy drinking will lead to an early death.
explanation.definitionFit: To portend is to be a warning sign of something to come, so it means foretell.

clue.text: Place to secure almost all hash and E, then start using gradually

indicators.note: to secure means to hold, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: to pin is to place or fix something in position

indicators.note: almost all means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: hash is cannabis
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A dealer's spot used for storing drugs before easing into taking them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' is a verb here, to fix in position, not a noun for a location.
explanation.definitionFit: To phase something in is to bring it into use step by step.

clue.text: Couple upset a Scottish hooligan? That takes guts!

parts.note: a duo is a couple

indicators.note: in a down answer upset means turned upside down, so read from bottom to top

parts.note: ned is Scottish slang for a young hooligan

explanation.surface: A pair who overturned a thug in Scotland showed real courage.
explanation.walkthrough: NED is Scottish slang for a hooligan, and 'upset' turns A NED into DENA. 'guts' looks like courage, but it means intestines.
explanation.definitionFit: The duodenum is the first part of the small intestine, so these are guts.

clue.text: Get stuck in toilet with individual snorting bit of Dexedrine

indicators.note: snorting means drawing in through the front, so the bit of the drug goes at the head of the word for individual

parts.note: bog is British slang for a toilet

indicators.note: a bit of the word means only its first letter is taken

parts.note: own means particular to an individual, as in one's own

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a toilet cubicle with a person sniffing a stimulant.
explanation.walkthrough: BOG is British slang for a toilet. The individual's OWN takes the D in at the front, as a nose does, to make DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Bog down is a phrasal verb for getting held up, so it means become stuck.

clue.text: In God's favour or damned?

definitions.meaning: ... is used as a mild curse, as in this ... car won't start

explanation.definitionFit: Blessed means holy, and also serves as a polite swear word like confounded.

clue.text: We don't like dressing fruits around plate endlessly

indicators.note: around means these letters surround the next piece

parts.note: nuts are fruits

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a dish is a plate

explanation.surface: Diners who refuse salad dressing on fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' looks like salad dressing but means putting clothes on; the definition speaks in the nudists' own voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudists choose to go without clothes, so they would say they don't like getting dressed.

clue.text: Pale ales finally necked by a Scottish woman

indicators.note: to neck something is to swallow it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: hen is a Scottish term of address for a woman

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word that comes before

explanation.surface: A woman in Scotland downing the last of her beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'necked' is British slang for drinking quickly. S, the last letter of 'ales', goes inside A HEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen describes a face drained of colour, the grey of ash, so it means pale.

clue.text: Revolutionary network of computers downs commercial server

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns over, so the result is read backwards
downs means swallows, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: LAN stands for local area network
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: A rebel computer system that brings down an advertising server.
explanation.walkthrough: 'server' looks like computing but means a tennis player, and 'Revolutionary' turns the whole container around.
explanation.definitionFit: Rafael Nadal is a Spanish tennis champion, and every tennis player takes turns to serve.

clue.text: All by myself and, oh, need to get jiggy!

indicators.note: getting jiggy is wild dancing or sexual activity, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Someone alone who sighs and admits they need some action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get jiggy' is slang for having sex, and here it scrambles AND OH NEED. The definition gives the answer a cheeky second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A task done one-handed is managed without help, so this is a playful version of all on my own.

clue.text: Hill, perhaps, rambler goes up

indicators.note: in a down answer goes up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a nomad wanders from place to place, a rambler

explanation.surface: A walker climbing a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hill' is a surname: Damon Hill, the British Formula One world champion. 'goes up' turns NOMAD upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Damon Hill was the 1996 Formula One champion, so his first name is an example.

clue.text: Really bad seeds spoilt red olives

indicators.note: spoilt olives are ruined, so the letters are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Olives gone off so badly that their stones are ruined too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seeds' looks literal, about olive stones, but a bad seed is a wicked person.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad seed is an idiom for a villain, so really bad seeds are wrongdoers.

clue.text: A couple of feet? Hoskins is bloody sizable primarily!

parts.note: the setter Hoskins would say of himself I am

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: The setter boasting about the size of his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter naming himself is a crossword convention for I or ME, so 'Hoskins is' gives I AM. 'feet' is meant here in the poetry sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An iamb is one metrical foot in verse, so two iambs make a pair of feet.

clue.text: Celebrity chef who uses loads of sauce?

definitions.text: Celebrity chef who uses loads of sauce?

parts.words: Celebrity chef who uses loads of sauce?
parts.note: sauce means both a cooking sauce and cheeky flirtation

explanation.surface: A TV cook who pours a lot of gravy and dressing over her food.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigella Lawson is a British TV cook famous for her flirty, suggestive presenting style. 'Sauce' also means cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigella Lawson is a famous TV cook known for her saucy, playful presenting style.

clue.text: Cads pinching nurse and daughter's butts

indicators.note: pinching means holding tight, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: a dog is slang for a worthless man, a cad
EN is the abbreviation for an Enrolled Nurse
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Rogues groping a nurse and a young woman's bottoms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butts' looks like bottoms, but it means cigarette ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog-ends is British slang for the stubs of smoked cigarettes, also called butts.
